comments.body:
## Correction: root cause established by bisect, and it is not what this ticket says

This ticket was filed saying the doctor failures were "re-exposed" by reverting the
out-of-scope `doctor.py` change in `985f`. That framing is **wrong**. These failures are a
**regression introduced by `985f` itself**, now live on `main` at `ddb1d953812`.

### Observation

At `ddb1d953812` (985f merged), `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py` reports 5 failures. All 5
reduce to a single cause:

```
rebar._commands._repair_pause.RepairPauseError:
  Error: doctor repair requires a configured git user.email
    at src/rebar/_commands/_repair_pause.py:117
```

Two of the five surface as `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1` —
downstream noise, because the command aborted and emitted no JSON. One surfaces as
`AssertionError: Regex pattern did not match. Actual message: 'Error: doctor repair requires a
configured git user.email'`.

### Bisect

Same file, same interpreter, same venv, at the parent commit `bed0718fba9` (immediately before
`985f`):

```
22 passed, 2 errors in 3.17s
```

**Zero failures.** The 2 errors are an artifact of the measurement, not the tree: the throwaway
bisect worktree borrowed the other worktree's venv, so the canonical-engine-root guard in
`tests/conftest.py:509` fired. They are not present in a normal checkout and are unrelated.

Post-`985f`: 5 failures. Pre-`985f`: 0 failures. The change is the cause.

### Mechanism

`tests/conftest.py:168` calls `scrub_ambient_git_config(os.environ)` from inside
`pytest_configure`. That is **session-wide and mutates the real process environment**, so every
subprocess spawned by any test for the rest of the session inherits the scrubbed environment.

The scrub is correct in intent — it removes the harness-injected command-scope
`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` / `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*` identity, which outranks both
repo-local config and a fake `HOME`, and which prevented identity-sensitive tests from
isolating themselves. That is what fixed the 20 git-identity nodeids.

But some tests were **relying on that ambient injected identity** to give their subprocess a
usable `user.email`. Those tests were never updated. After the scrub they have no identity at
all, and `doctor --repair` correctly refuses to run without one.

So the scrub is right and the consumers are wrong: a test that needs a working git identity
must establish one explicitly rather than inheriting whatever the harness happened to inject.
That is also the more robust design, because it does not depend on the harness.

### Why the original census missed these

The census of 51 sandbox failures was taken against unmodified `origin/main`, where the ambient
injected identity was still present. These 5 could not appear there. They are new, not
uncounted.

### Why the earlier measurement said 32

Patch set 1 of `985f` also changed `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py`, which masked these. That
change was correctly reverted as out of scope, which is what made the failures visible — hence
the original "re-exposed" reading. The revert did not *cause* them; it stopped hiding them.

### Scope correction

Raising to **P1**: this is a regression on `main`, not a pre-existing wart. The remedy is to
give the affected tests an explicit git identity, not to weaken or narrow the scrub, and not to
reinstate the `doctor.py` change that masked it.

Related but distinct, and **not** part of this ticket:
`tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py::test_a_contended_fcntl_leg_reads_as_held` fails with
`PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted` from `multiprocessing.SemLock` — that is
the sandbox SemLock class owned by `0eba-cfd8-34b0-4cb7`.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`tests/conftest.py` scrubs the harness-injected command-scope git identity from the **real
process environment** at session start. Tests that depended on that ambient identity to give a
subprocess a usable `user.email` now have none, and `doctor --repair` correctly refuses to run.

Introduced by `985f-0ec5-a61c-46ee`, live on `main` at `ddb1d953812`.

## Observation

At `ddb1d953812`, `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py` reports 5 failures:

```
tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py::test_repair_force_writes_the_pre_repair_tag_and_repoints_it
tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py::test_run_repair_does_not_hold_a_lock_that_blocks_its_own_writes
tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py::test_json_output_carries_the_documented_finding_fields
tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py::test_repair_refuses_while_a_reconciler_pass_is_in_flight
tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py::test_unrepairable_finding_leaves_its_edge_and_the_run_continues
```

All 5 reduce to one cause:

```
rebar._commands._repair_pause.RepairPauseError:
  Error: doctor repair requires a configured git user.email
    at src/rebar/_commands/_repair_pause.py:117
```

Two surface as `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1` — downstream
noise, because the command aborted and emitted no JSON. One surfaces as `AssertionError: Regex
pattern did not match. Actual message: 'Error: doctor repair requires a configured git
user.email'`.

## Root cause — established by bisect, not inferred

Same file, same interpreter, same venv, at the parent commit `bed0718fba9`: **0 failures**
(`22 passed`). At `ddb1d953812`: **5 failures**.

`tests/conftest.py:168` calls `scrub_ambient_git_config(os.environ)` from inside
`pytest_configure`. That is session-wide and mutates the real process environment, so every
subprocess spawned by any test for the remainder of the session inherits the scrubbed
environment.

The scrub itself is **correct and must not be weakened**. It removes the harness-injected
`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` / `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*` command-scope identity, which
outranks both repo-local config and a fake `HOME`. Removing it is what allowed 20 previously
failing identity-sensitive tests to isolate themselves.

The defect is that some tests were **relying on that injected identity** to supply a working
`user.email` to a subprocess, and were never updated. A test that needs a working git identity
must establish one explicitly rather than inheriting whatever the harness happened to inject —
which is also the more robust design, since it does not depend on the harness.

## Why the original 51-failure census did not include these

The census was taken against unmodified `origin/main`, where the ambient injected identity was
still present. These failures could not appear there. They are new, not previously uncounted.

Patch set 1 of `985f` also changed `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py`, which masked them. That
change was correctly reverted as out of scope, which is what made them visible. The revert did
not cause them.

## Explicitly out of scope

- Weakening, narrowing, or conditionalising `scrub_ambient_git_config`. The scrub is the fix
  for 20 other tests.
- Reinstating the `doctor.py` change from `985f` patch set 1. It masked the symptom and was
  out of scope for that ticket and this one.
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py::test_a_contended_fcntl_leg_reads_as_held`, which
  fails with `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted` from
  `multiprocessing.SemLock`. That is the sandbox SemLock class owned by `0eba-cfd8-34b0-4cb7`.

## Approach

Give the affected tests an explicit, known-good git identity for the subprocesses they spawn,
established by the test rather than inherited from the environment. Prefer a single shared
helper alongside `scrub_ambient_git_config` in `tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py` over repeating
identity setup in each test, so the two concerns — remove ambient identity, establish a
deliberate one — sit together and are individually testable.

Confirm whether any test outside `test_doctor.py` has the same latent dependency on ambient
identity, and cover those too, so this does not recur one file at a time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The 5 enumerated `test_doctor.py` nodeids pass under the agent sandbox. Verified by
      `pytest` on those 5 nodeids exiting 0, with the summary line recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] The 20 git-identity nodeids fixed by `985f` still pass, proving the scrub was not
      weakened. Verified by `pytest` on those nodeids exiting 0, with the summary recorded.
- [ ] A test asserts that a subprocess spawned by the shared identity helper sees a configured
      `user.email`. Verified by that test failing when the helper is stubbed to a no-op.
- [ ] `scrub_ambient_git_config` still removes every injected command-scope identity variable.
      Verified by the existing scrub test in `tests/test_sandbox_capabilities_985f.py` passing
      unchanged.
- [ ] Any other test depending on ambient injected identity is identified and fixed, or its
      absence is demonstrated. Verified by a recorded search over tests spawning git
      subprocesses and the resulting nodeid list.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass, reported with exit status.
- [ ] Full `make test` under the agent sandbox reports no failure whose cause is a missing
      configured git identity. Verified by running it and recording the failure composition.
